explainer: The single best AI-bubble bellwether is the rental price of an installed Nvidia GPU, measured in dollars per GPU-hour, and specifically the H100: it is the daily marginal clearing price for AI compute, it is published by independent indexes (Silicon Data's SDH100RT, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index), and a CME futures contract on it is pending: the CFTC extended its review to November 9, 2026, so a forward curve is coming but not yet listed. Right now it is saying the opposite of discounting: the Silicon Data index sits at $2.75/hr (Sep 30), a new high, one-year contract rates rose about 40% from $1.70 to $2.35 between October 2025 and March 2026, spot has run at roughly twice contract, and a four-year-old chip is renting for more than it did a year ago while CoreWeave says it has contracted 2020-vintage GPUs out to 2029 at full price. Pair it with three things: neocloud credit spreads (CoreWeave's July loan cleared at SOFR+550 for a 10.44% yield with maintenance covenants, and its CDS implies roughly a coin-flip default probability), which is the financing leg and the one signal already flashing red; server DRAM and HBM contract-price momentum (+13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 after +93-98% in 1Q26, with 4Q26 guided to only +3-8%), because memory is the first physical input that will roll over; and hyperscaler backlog growth versus capex growth (Microsoft commercial RPO +84%, Oracle RPO +363%, roughly $2.4 trillion of committed cloud backlog against about $1 trillion of 2026 capex), because the bubble only deflates if the buyers stop signing. Over the next one to two quarters watch Nvidia's August 26 print for gross margin and customer concentration (three direct customers were already 54% of revenue), the shape of the CME H100/B200 curve if the CFTC clears it in November (a steep backwardation would be the first public forecast of discounting), whether 4Q26 memory contract talks and 2027 HBM4 pricing turn negative, and what ERCOT's December audit says about how much of Texas's 474 GW interconnection queue is phantom demand. The threshold that would flip the call is simple: the H100 index sustained below about $2.00/hr, or spot trading below the one-year contract rate, while Blackwell and Rubin volumes keep arriving; until then compute is being sold at a premium, not a discount, and the risk lives in who is borrowing to build it rather than in the price of the product.

indicators.name: H100 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index; 1-yr contract and spot)
indicators.value: Silicon Data SDH100RT $2.83/hr as of Oct 11 (+0.7% 7d), first dip in the series this month, down 2c from $2.85 Oct 9. H200 $3.44 (+4.2% 7d) vs $3.39; A100 $1.53 (+0.7%); MI300X $2.64 (0.0%). CME H100/B200 futures: CFTC extended review 45 days, launch Nov 9 or later.
indicators.why: Hopper spot firmed through the Oct 8 OpenAI revenue scare: every Silicon Data index rose over the week, so rented compute is still being bid, not discounted.
indicators.watch: Bearish flip if SDH100RT prints below ~$2.00 for a month or spot drops under the 1-yr contract rate. Next: whether the Oct 8 demand scare shows up in the index with a lag, and the CME/CFTC listing decision.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 9: the headline index slipped 2c to $2.83 (Oct 11 reading) and the 7-day gain narrowed from +2.5% to +0.7%, so the Oct 8 OpenAI scare may be showing up with a lag, but the week is still positive. H200 rose 5c to $3.44 and its 7-day change jumped to +4.2%; A100 and MI300X were unchanged. The CFTC review is now re-verified: BigGo Finance (Sep 23) reports a 45-day extension that pushes CME's H100 and B200 rental futures to Nov 9 or later, citing price-transparency and manipulation concerns; ICE is planning a rival contract with no date. Trend and signal held: one 2c dip is noise against a $2.00 trigger. Watch this week whether the index keeps slipping after the ASML (Oct 14), Anthropic (Oct 14) and TSMC (Oct 15) readouts.

indicators.name: B200 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index) and B200/H100 ratio
indicators.value: Silicon Data B200 $5.93 as of Oct 11 (+1.0% 7d), unchanged from Oct 9; B300 $6.67 (+2.2% 7d) vs $6.71. B200/H100 ratio 2.10x (5.93/2.83), up from 2.08x because Hopper dipped. Both well above the $4.50 and 2x triggers.
indicators.why: Blackwell rents rose again and B300 rose faster than B200; the newest capacity is still clearing at a premium, which is what a supply-constrained market looks like.
indicators.watch: Bearish if B200 drops below $4.50 or the B200/H100 ratio falls under 2x. Also watch whether B300 keeps widening its premium over B200 as Rubin nears.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 9: B200 was flat at $5.93 and its 7-day change eased from +1.2% to +1.0%; B300 fell 4c to $6.67 though its 7-day change is +2.2%. The ratio went back to 2.10x because H100 dipped, not because Blackwell rose. The FAQ's stale $5.45 is again ignored. CME B200 futures sit in the same CFTC review as H100, launch Nov 9 or later (BigGo Finance, Sep 23). Trend and signal held; watch whether TSMC's Oct 15 results and any Rubin timing commentary pull B300 rents down further.

indicators.name: Hopper residual value: A100 index floor, used H100 prices, GPU useful-life accounting
indicators.value: A100 index $1.53 Oct 11 (+0.7% 7d; trigger $1.50), unchanged from Oct 9. Silicon Data residual study (Jan 30 data): used H100 ~65-75% of new at 2 yrs, 45-55% at 3 yrs; median resale mid-$20Ks late-2025, low end $12-16K. No new Hopper impairments or useful-life changes seen Oct 10-12.
indicators.why: A100 is still a cent or three above the $1.50 floor and ticked up this week; the residual-value question is unresolved rather than deteriorating.
indicators.watch: A100 index under $1.50; any hyperscaler or neocloud shortening GPU useful life or booking a Hopper impairment in Q3 results (late Oct onward); used H100 SXM asks drifting below $18K.
indicators.note: No new reading since Oct 9 beyond the A100 index, which held at $1.53, still 3c above the floor. H200 rents rose 4.2% over the week to $3.44, which supports Hopper-generation values. No used-H100 price reports, impairments or useful-life changes were found Oct 10-12; the $18-27K used SXM range and lender underwriting assumptions are carried forward. Trend and signal held. Watch Q3 results from late October for any hyperscaler or neocloud shortening GPU lives.

indicators.name: Data-centre cost per GW and the cost of capital (10-yr Treasury)
indicators.value: No new campus $/GW prints Oct 10-12 (last: Vera Rubin ~$47B/GW, gas campus ~$60B/GW, Project Jupiter ~$67B/GW). 10-yr Treasury held at Friday's 5.24% par close; bond market shut Monday for Columbus Day. Startup Fortune notes the 10-yr touched 5.304% this month and a $39B auction cleared at 5.30%.
indicators.why: Build cost per GW is unchanged and the cost of capital eased 4bp off the Oct 7 high but is still above 5.2%, so every GW is funded at the most expensive rates in two decades.
indicators.watch: 10-yr back above 5.30%; any new campus announcement implying more than ~$60B/GW; Amazon's newly disclosed data-centre deal terms now that it is dropping NDAs.
indicators.note: No new reading since Oct 9: bonds were closed Monday so the 10-year stays at Friday's 5.24% par yield. The cost of funding campuses got worse at the margin, though: FT (via Coinpaper, Oct 11) citing Morgan Stanley says global AI-related debt issuance fell from $113B in June to $23B in September, with US investment-grade AI issuance at zero in September. Bloomberg and FT (via Startup Fortune, Oct 11) report banks are exploring risk transfers on $38B of construction debt for Oracle-leased Texas and Wisconsin campuses. No new $/GW figure was found. Trend and signal held; watch Treasury reopening Tuesday and whether any campus refinances at wider spreads.

indicators.name: Memory prices: DRAM spot and contract, HBM, Samsung and Micron readthrough
indicators.value: TrendForce spot Oct 12: DDR5 16Gb $59.43 (+0.91%, vs $58.90 Oct 9), DDR4 16Gb $83.89 (+0.29%), DDR4 8Gb $46.08 (-0.23%). Samsung -3.2%, SK hynix -3.6% in Monday's Kospi selloff (2pm). Contract table still 2H Aug. TrendForce 4Q26 DRAM contract +10-15%; 2027 HBM contract +70-140%.
indicators.why: Spot DRAM kept inching up through the AI selloff and Samsung's preliminary profit confirms the pricing power; the only soft spot is demand destruction in PCs, which does not touch server DRAM or HBM.
indicators.watch: TrendForce's October contract-price update (the contract table is still 2H Aug); Samsung full Q3 results late Oct; any sign DDR4 16Gb spot rolls over from $83-84; MU move after the Oct 8 chip selloff.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 9: DDR5 16Gb spot rose 53c to $59.43 and DDR4 16Gb 25c to $83.89 on Monday's Asia session, both new series highs; DDR4 8Gb eased 11c. The stocks went the other way: Bloomingbit reports the Kospi down 3.17% at 2pm Oct 12 with Samsung -3.24% and SK hynix -3.63% and foreigners net sellers of W1.56T, citing the OpenAI revenue report and Middle East risk. Investing.com adds CXMT plans a new server memory product by end-2026, a first Chinese challenge in server DRAM. Prices, not shares, drive this indicator, so trend and signal hold. Watch TrendForce's October contract update, the Micron Taoyuan union rally Oct 19, and Samsung's full Q3 later this month.

indicators.name: Power bottleneck: ERCOT/PJM queues, Texas permit freeze, turbine backlog
indicators.value: No new Texas prints Oct 10-12: ERCOT 474 GW large-load queue (420.8 GW data centres), TCEQ data-centre permit freeze since Sep 21, compliance report due Oct 19, ERCOT review targeted by December. Texas Water Development Board progress report due Oct 14. PJM capacity advisory in effect Oct 12-13. GE Vernova 116 GW gas backlog unchanged.
indicators.why: Grid capacity is still the binding constraint on how fast compute can be deployed: PJM is issuing tight-conditions advisories in October and only just fast-tracking its first new generators, which keeps existing GPU capacity scarce.
indicators.watch: Texas TCEQ compliance report Oct 19; ERCOT Batch Zero timing; FERC action on PJM's large-load curtailment proposal; GE Vernova Q3 backlog (late Oct).
indicators.note: No new reading since Oct 9. A law-firm summary (Global ELR, Oct 5) confirms the freeze covers both ERCOT interconnection and all TCEQ permits until ERCOT's audit ends, now targeted for December, and adds a Texas Water Development Board progress report due Oct 14. PJM's Oct 12-13 warm-weather capacity advisory is in effect today. Nothing new on turbine backlogs. Trend and signal held; the hard dates this week are TWDB on Oct 14 and TCEQ's compliance report on Oct 19.

indicators.name: Capex vs backlog: hyperscaler spend, RPO, AI-lab commitments and buyer revenue quality
indicators.value: OpenAI annualised revenue 'approaching $50B' (FT, Oct 8) vs ~$70B assumed; Bloomberg says $70B+ by year-end. AI-related debt issuance fell to $23B in September from $113B in June (Morgan Stanley via FT). Nvidia in early talks to buy or deepen its stake in Reflection AI (FT, Oct 10). Anthropic investor session Oct 14.
indicators.why: The commitments did not change but the biggest buyer's revenue base is ~30% smaller than the market assumed, so backlog coverage by customer revenue got worse on paper; it is an accounting gap, not a demand drop, which keeps this neutral rather than bearish.
indicators.watch: Anthropic investor session Oct 14; OpenAI's $30B round at $1.4T pre-money closing or re-priced; Q3 hyperscaler capex guides late Oct; whether Bloomberg's reported $70B+ year-end run-rate is confirmed by OpenAI.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 9: no new revenue or capex numbers, but two financing signals. FT (via Coinpaper, Oct 11) citing Morgan Stanley says AI-related debt issuance fell nearly 80% from June to September and about $466B was borrowed in the first nine months, so the buyers are slowing new borrowing even as backlog stands. FT (via PYMNTS, Oct 11) reports Nvidia is in early talks to acquire or invest further in Reflection AI, where it already has $800M; inference: another case of the chip supplier funding its own demand. No OpenAI round or Anthropic update was found Oct 10-12. Trend and signal held. Watch Anthropic's Oct 14 session and TSMC's Oct 15 capex guide.

indicators.name: Neocloud credit: CoreWeave leverage and bond yields, neocloud and chip financing

indicators.name: Nvidia data centre: revenue, margin, concentration, backstops and demand signals

FT Oct 10: Nvidia in early talks to acquire Reflection AI or invest more (already $800M; Reflection valued $25B in March); acqui-hire structure possible.
